what: eBay runs an online marketplace. It does not own the goods: buyers and sellers transact and eBay takes a fee. It has moved toward categories where its format works best, such as collectibles, car parts, refurbished electronics and luxury watches.
customers: Individual and small-business sellers, and buyers looking for used, rare or hard-to-find items.
moat: Depth of supply in categories where items are one of a kind, which cannot be replicated by a retailer holding stock.
risks: Total goods sold on the platform has grown very slowly for years
Amazon and social marketplaces compete for both buyers and sellers
Debt of about $6 billion against $1 billion of cash
opportunities: Operating margin of 21% and return on invested capital of 17% are strong
Advertising revenue grows faster than the marketplace itself
Focused categories such as watches and car parts are growing while the rest is flat
watch: Gross merchandise volume growth and advertising revenue as a share of the total.
